note: Machine-readable registry for the first real timetable collection phase of v3. This is the first concrete train-data intake layer for Tokyo-area JR and private operators. It records which operators are ready to collect now, which official sources to target first, and which existing v2 ingestion scripts can be reused.

operators.notes: Tokyo core weekday collection now completed for the first JR East conventional batch using 32 official timetable pages across Tokyo, Shinjuku, Ueno, Shinagawa, Yokohama, and Chiba. Output: data/v3_tokyo_jreast_core_weekday_train_instances.json (3747 merged instances).
Already proven in v2; remains the Tokyo Shinkansen-side timetable base for v3.

All Tokyo Metro lines should enter together in v3 phase 1. The public station site now confirms an official redirect chain into the Metro timetable web app at transfer.tokyometro.jp, and the official `/api/timetable` plus `/api/stop` endpoints are now verified. The weekday collector has produced `17099` train instances across `370` source pages in data/v3_tokyo_tokyo_metro_weekday_train_instances.json.gz.

Public Toei GTFS has now been collected into data/v3_tokyo_toei_weekday_train_instances.json for a weekday service day (2026-04-13), producing 2818 train instances across Asakusa, Mita, Shinjuku, Oedo, Nippori-Toneri, and Toden Arakawa. A small fallback_physical_stations block is included for unresolved stop-name variants that still need merging back into the canonical station seed.

All Tokyu lines enter together. The current Navitime-backed collector has produced an audited weekday batch of 1373 train instances in data/v3_tokyo_tokyu_weekday_train_instances.json, with no remaining stop-signature duplicates.

All Odakyu lines enter together. The official station-page collector has produced an audited weekday batch of 1840 train instances in data/v3_tokyo_odakyu_weekday_train_instances.json, with duplicate stop-list overcount removed.

All Keio lines should be collected together if Keio enters timetable scope. The official `/api/keio/timetable/{station}/{line}/{direction}` and `/api/keio/stops/{station}/{line}` endpoints are now verified, and the company-wide weekday collector has produced `1924` train instances across `70` source pages in data/v3_tokyo_keio_weekday_train_instances.json.

Keikyu enters company-wide. The official station-page collector now resolves T5 hour tables and T7 single-train stop tables into an audited weekday batch of 1328 train instances in data/v3_tokyo_keikyu_weekday_train_instances.json.

Tobu enters as a whole company per axiom. The Navitime-backed collector has produced an audited weekday batch of 5958 train instances in data/v3_tokyo_tobu_weekday_train_instances.json after removing second-layer line-context duplicates.

Seibu enters as a whole-company timetable target. The current collector has produced an audited weekday checkpoint of 1554 train instances in data/v3_tokyo_seibu_weekday_train_instances.json after stop-signature dedupe.

Keisei enters as a whole-company target. The current official timetable collector has produced an audited weekday checkpoint of 1434 train instances in data/v3_tokyo_keisei_weekday_train_instances.json after stop-signature dedupe.

operators.notes: Rinkai Line weekday collection is now available in data/v3_tokyo_rinkai_weekday_train_instances.json with 542 train instances built from the official Shin-Kiba and Osaki timetable pages plus 550 linked train-detail pages. The current batch keeps the full Rinkai segment of through-running trains while preserving their real beyond-Rinkai headsigns such as Kawagoe and Omiya.

A first weekday batch is now available in data/v3_tokyo_yurikamome_weekday_train_instances.json, built from all 16 official station timetable PDFs plus N02 station geometry. The current batch reconstructs 483 weekday train instances and already preserves Ariake short-turn behavior, though the terminal-time inference should still be treated as first-batch quality rather than final perfect reconstruction.

A first weekday batch is now available in data/v3_tokyo_tokyo_monorail_weekday_train_instances.json, built from the official Navitime-backed stop-sections endpoint plus N02 station geometry. The current batch reconstructs 429 weekday train instances across all 11 stations on the Haneda Airport Line.

A first weekday batch is now available in data/v3_tokyo_tama_monorail_weekday_train_instances.json, built from all official timetable PDFs plus N02 station geometry. The current batch reconstructs 507 weekday train instances across 19 stations.

A first weekday batch is now available in data/v3_tokyo_tsukuba_express_weekday_train_instances.json, built from the official Navitime-powered train timetable API and N02 station geometry. The current batch reconstructs 463 weekday train instances across the full Tsukuba Express line.
